question.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $6{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}-60y+8x=-122?$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}-60y+8x & =-122 \\ 6{y}^{2}-60y-4{x}^{2}+8x & =-122 \\ 6[{y}^{2}-10y]-4[{x}^{2}-2x] & =-122 \\ 6[(y-5)^{2}-25]-4[(x-1)^{2}-1] & =-122 \\ 6(y-5)^{2}-150-4(x-1)^{2}+4 & =-122 \\ 6(y-5)^{2}-4(x-1)^{2} & =-122+150-4 \\ 6(y-5)^{2}-4(x-1)^{2} & =24 \\ \frac{(y-5)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{6} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-5)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{(\sqrt{6})^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(1,5).$
